source: BK5 printed p.24 = book5-6.pdf PDF p.30 (Experiment 13: Multiple Point Control), wire table image-read at 400 dpi (round-1 fidelity review, 2026-10-14), all 28 entries match, 4 columns column-major; errata.pdf p.3 carries no Experiment 13 entry (the Book V pages 21-22 note ER-33 concerns M10 matrix connections in Experiment 12 and applies to no wire here; the page 24 correction is Experiment 14 only); Step 7 speculative derivation from topology
note: Step 7 speculative fixture (derivation A): every until is derived by hand from the 28-wire topology and the p.24 rule, not printed. No erratum touches this program. Printed setup (BK5 p.24): 'Set all slide switches to the RIGHT. Turn power on.' The page prints no order or count for the operations; the script exercises all twelve 'locations' once, in the sentence's order: pushbuttons 1-6 (each pushed and released), then slide switches 1-6 (each LEFT and back RIGHT). Topology: the twelve rest contacts (pushbutton N.C., slide switch set 2 RIGHT) form one series loop from + to node Q (6W/6H/5J); relays 5 and 6 form a two-relay binary toggle whose coils share far end F (5F/6F/5H); light 4 follows relay 6 through 6L(+)-6K. Opening the loop (push, or slide LEFT) flips relay 6 and so light 4; closing it (release, or slide back RIGHT) moves relay 5 to match, which arms the next flip. Derived reading of the rule: one complete operation (push and release, or LEFT and back RIGHT) toggles light 4; the visible change lands on the push or the LEFT move. Light 4 starts off at power-up (not printed). Checkpoints use an until with maxMs 1500 after each settle because settle can return while a filament is still in transit (open-questions.md O-C28). Lamps 5 and 6 are asserted only where their node sits on + (full rail) or is dead; where a lamp sits behind a coil its class depends on profile constants and is not asserted.

script.cite: BK5 printed p.24 = book5-6.pdf PDF p.30 multiple-point-control rule, all slide switches RIGHT and power turned on, before any operation; derived from topology: the 12-contact series loop runs + (6+/6Z) through every pushbutton N.C. contact (6Z-6Y, 6Y/5Z ... 2Y/1Z, 1Z-1Y), 1Y/1V, then every slide switch set 2 RIGHT contact (1V-1W, 1W/2V ... 5W/6V, 6V-6W) to the node Q = 6W/6H/5J; F = 5F/6F/5H is the common far end of coils 5 and 6; E5 = 5E/5A/6G carries output lamp 5 (5A-5B, 5B on -) beside indicator lamp 5 (5E-5C, 5C on -); E6 = 6E/6A/6J likewise carries output lamp 6 and indicator lamp 6 (6C on -); light 4 (4A-4B, 4B on -) is fed only by 6L(+)-6K; loop closed so Q is on +; relay 5 released puts F on Q through 5H-5J and relay 6 released puts E6 on Q through 6H-6J, so coil 6 has + at both ends; coil 5 runs F(+)-coil-E5 and through the two lamps on E5 to -, so relay 5 pulls in and then holds itself through 5G(+)-5H; E6 sits on + so output lamp 6 has full rail; 6L-6K is open so light 4 is dark
script.quote: Light 4 may be turned on or off by pushing any pushbutton or by moving any slide switch to the LEFT and then back to the RIGHT. (Note: lights 5 and 6 are wired into the control circuit.)

script.cite: BK5 printed p.24 = book5-6.pdf PDF p.30 multiple-point-control rule, operation 1 of 12, pushbutton 1 pushed and held; derived from topology: the 12-contact series loop runs + (6+/6Z) through every pushbutton N.C. contact (6Z-6Y, 6Y/5Z ... 2Y/1Z, 1Z-1Y), 1Y/1V, then every slide switch set 2 RIGHT contact (1V-1W, 1W/2V ... 5W/6V, 6V-6W) to the node Q = 6W/6H/5J; F = 5F/6F/5H is the common far end of coils 5 and 6; E5 = 5E/5A/6G carries output lamp 5 (5A-5B, 5B on -) beside indicator lamp 5 (5E-5C, 5C on -); E6 = 6E/6A/6J likewise carries output lamp 6 and indicator lamp 6 (6C on -); light 4 (4A-4B, 4B on -) is fed only by 6L(+)-6K; loop open so Q is cut from +; relay 6 released joins Q to E6 only (5J is open with relay 5 operated); F is on + through 5G-5H, so coil 6 runs F(+)-coil-E6 and through the two lamps on E6 to - and relay 6 pulls in; 6L(+)-6K then lights light 4; relay 5 still holds through 5G-5H (its coil runs F(+)-E5 and the lamps)
script.quote: Light 4 may be turned on or off by pushing any pushbutton or by moving any slide switch to the LEFT and then back to the RIGHT.
